wikipediaArticleRead.support: L124–130 identifies Rezon as son of Eliada, a former follower of Hadadezer, and an adversary of Solomon. It notes the proposed identification with Hezion as an old scholarly theory, not a fact; the profile does not adopt it.

sourceTextExcerpts.text: God raised up an adversary to him, Rezon the son of Eliada, who had fled from his lord, Hadadezer king of Zobah.
He gathered men to himself, and became captain over a troop, when David killed them of Zobah. They went to Damascus and lived there, and reigned in Damascus.
He was an adversary to Israel all the days of Solomon, in addition to the mischief of Hadad. He abhorred Israel, and reigned over Syria.
